Born: December 27, 1995, 9:16 PM local time, Manhattan, New York, USA. Source: Astro-Databank, Rodden rating AA.

The AA rating means the time comes from a birth certificate or an equally official record, so the rising sign, the Midheaven and the houses below can be read at face value. Open Timothée Chalamet's chart on Astrolas to follow along.

One feature runs the whole chart. Five of the ten planets, Sun, Mercury, Mars, Uranus and Neptune, sit in the same sign and the same house: Capricorn, in the 5th house. The Astrolas library ties the 5th house to creativity, performance and romance, and Capricorn to discipline, ambition and early-arriving maturity. Put those two together and the chart reads like a brief for a working actor who treats craft as a serious, structured pursuit rather than a hobby. He earned an Oscar nomination for Call Me by Your Name at 22, then went on to lead a film franchise, Dune, and a biopic, A Complete Unknown, playing Bob Dylan, that earned him a second nomination.

muc.ten: Five planets in Capricorn, in the 5th house of performance
doan: The Sun sits at 5°52' Capricorn, Mercury at 24°08', Mars at 21°08', Uranus at 29°08', and Neptune at 24°32', all in the same sign and the 5th house.

The library's Capricorn Sun reads as serious, organized and more determined than most, maturing early and finding greater fulfillment with age, driven by responsibility and a clear sense of ambition, with a career that tends to reward structure, endurance and long-term thinking. Its note on the 5th house separately describes a love of performance, competitive activity and creative self-expression, work that doubles as a kind of offspring when it isn't literal children. Five planets landing in exactly that house, all disciplined by Capricorn, is a hard combination to find elsewhere in a chart: structure aimed squarely at the stage.

Mercury in Capricorn adds a practical, sequential mind, one that weighs both the fine detail and the larger plan before acting, and that the library says tends toward leadership and authority once the discipline pays off. Mars in Capricorn restrains its energy until it's needed, then applies it with endurance rather than a sudden burst, aimed at status and long-term security rather than quick wins. Both readings describe patience built for a career measured in decades, not a single viral moment.

The chart's second-tightest aspect also touches this cluster: Uranus trine the Midheaven, an orb of just 0°47'. The library has no text for it yet, so it's worth naming only as a fact, a quick, unconventional line running straight from the Capricorn planets to the career point of the chart.

muc.ten: Mercury conjunct Neptune: the tightest aspect in the chart
doan: Mercury and Neptune are conjunct at an orb of just 0°24', the tightest contact anywhere in the chart.

The library reads this as a visionary mind, someone who thinks in pictures rather than words and can move an audience through language or image alone, with real creative pull toward art and writing. It also carries a caution: when a thought turns rigid, reality gets harder to see clearly, particularly around contracts and money, and the advice is to check things carefully rather than trust instinct alone. His choice of roles, from an arthouse debut to a spice-opera franchise to playing Bob Dylan, reads as a career built on instinct for which story is worth the risk, not on an obvious commercial formula.

muc.ten: Mercury conjunct Mars: quick, combative wit
doan: Mercury and Mars are also conjunct, at an orb of 3°01'.

Astrolas reads this pairing as a sharp, decisive mind with real eloquence, capable of winning most arguments even without knowing the whole subject, and strong enough in public speaking to shine in front of an audience. The library's caution is a short temper and a tendency toward snap decisions. It's a fair description of an actor known for quick, candid press interviews as much as for his range on screen.

muc.ten: Mars conjunct Neptune: talent wrapped in mystery
doan: Mars and Neptune are conjunct too, at an orb of 3°25'.

The library reads this as talent paired with a magnetism that's hard to pin down, the kind that draws people in without a clear explanation why. Its caution is a tendency to scatter focus, chase idealistic goals, or act indirectly rather than head-on, leaving even the person who has it unsure of their own role at times. The flip side, in the library's reading, is strong intuition that can work like inspiration or healing for other people. Critics have described his screen presence in similar terms for years: soulful, elusive, hard to fully explain.

muc.ten: Moon in Pisces, in the 8th house: depth kept private
doan: The Moon sits at 27°20' Pisces in the 8th house.

The library's Pisces Moon is deeply sensitive, easily absorbing other people's emotions, drawn to art and intuition, and prone to blurring the line between imagination and reality. In the 8th house specifically, it describes emotion running deeper than most people show, financial security mattering a great deal to emotional stability, and a strong sixth sense that's useful when paired with real information rather than relied on alone.

That combination, a deep inner life paired with an 8th house instinct for privacy, lines up with his well-documented reluctance to discuss his personal life in interviews, keeping the public conversation on the work rather than on himself.

muc.ten: Jupiter and Pluto in Sagittarius, in the 4th house of home
doan: Jupiter sits at 28°35' Sagittarius, Pluto at 1°49' Sagittarius, both in the 4th house of home and family. They're not close enough in degree to form a tight aspect, but the shared sign and house still matter.

Jupiter in Sagittarius is its own ruling sign, one of the library's most fortunate placements, bringing optimism, generosity and a pull toward travel, philosophy and knowledge. In the 4th house, it adds a deep attachment to family and a wish for a spacious, comfortable home. Pluto in Sagittarius is generational, tied to the internet era's expansion of knowledge and global connection across the late 1990s and 2000s; in the 4th house it turns personal, describing home as a space held under careful, private control. He has an older sister, Pauline Chalamet, also an actress, and has spoken about his family's influence on his path into the arts without turning that into tabloid material.

muc.ten: Saturn in Pisces, and Virgo rising
doan: Saturn sits at 19°09' Pisces in the 7th house. The library reads Saturn in Pisces as deep intuition paired with a real challenge around material success, someone who learns through hard circumstance to trade escapism for resilience, often finding meaning through philosophy, literature or art. In the 7th house of partnership, it describes someone serious and cautious about commitment, who tends to commit only once truly certain and may settle down later than most.

The Ascendant is Virgo at 3°13', though the Astrolas library doesn't yet have an entry for Virgo rising on its own. Two aspects to the angles are also missing text: Pluto square the Ascendant, an orb of 1°23', and the Sun trine the Ascendant, an orb of 2°39'. Both are facts worth naming, not placements this article can read into.

muc.ten: What the chart adds up to
doan: Nothing here explains why a particular performance lands. What the chart does show is where the weight sits: five planets disciplined by Capricorn, all pushed into the house of performance, a Mercury-Neptune pairing built for instinct over formula, and a Moon that keeps its depth mostly out of view.
Open Timothée Chalamet's chart on Astrolas, find the Capricorn cluster in the 5th house on the wheel, then compare it with a chart you know.
Virgo, at 3°13', based on his AA-rated birth time of 9:16 PM.
His Sun is at 5°52' Capricorn in the 5th house. His Moon is at 27°20' Pisces in the 8th house.

Five planets, the Sun, Mercury, Mars, Uranus and Neptune, all in Capricorn and all in the 5th house of performance and creativity. It's one of the densest single clusters you'll find in any chart, and it points straight at a disciplined, high-output creative career.
